description: A comprehensive suite of earthquake catalogues for the 2016-2017 Central Italy seismic sequence is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Lauro Chiaraluce et al. The protracted nature of the 2016-2017 central Italy seismic sequence, with multiple damaging earthquakes spaced over months, presented serious challenges for the duty seismologists and emergency managers as they assimilated the growing sequence to advise the local population. Coverage: national (IT); published in 2022. The formats are not stated in the sources read. The data are held in Oak Ridge National Laboratory and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence of the data is not stated in the sources read (the paper itself is open access). Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support emergency-service and public-facility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
